_comment: Demo data for ?demo=1. Every company below is invented. Any resemblance to a real business is coincidental, and none of these figures are real. Swap them freely, or delete the file and demo mode simply renders empty.

companies.consumerProduct: Lumière Atelier, an in-app styling assistant

quote.text: AI is no longer a project inside this house. It is how the house runs.
quote.speaker: R. Delacroix

companies.notes: Textbook performer. Rhetoric and shipped output move together, and the ROI figure is stated on the call rather than briefed to press.
The most underrated profile in the demo set. Four confirmed tools in production and almost no board narrative. Watch for a rhetoric jump at the next capital markets day.

quote.text: Every part of this business will be reimagined around artificial intelligence.
quote.speaker: H. Osei

companies.notes: Narrative-led, textbook case. Strongest AI language in the demo set, one confirmed tool, and it is still in beta. The gap between the narrative and the shipped list is the story.
Quietly competent. Quantified saving disclosed, no consumer-facing product, no interest in an AI narrative beyond the numbers.
Smallest company in the set and the fastest mover. Consumer tool is genuinely live rather than a pilot.

companies.roiFigure: AI-attributed contribution not separated: the platform is the model
companies.notes: Renders off-matrix. Scoring a business whose core product is a model on the same two axes as a grocer flatters nobody, so it sits outside the quadrants.
No AI language in the annual report and no confirmed tools. Absence is disclosed rather than guessed at, and absence is a finding.
Two confirmed tools, both internal, both mentioned once in a sustainability appendix rather than the main deck.

pulse.headline: Verdant Grocers extends fresh-waste forecasting to all 1,900 stores
pulse.source: Verdant Grocers FY26 Q1 trading update
pulse.soWhat: So what: the quietest company in the set now has the widest deployment. Ask why the board still will not talk about it.

pulse.headline: Northwind Apparel names first Chief AI Officer, Fit Finder still in beta
pulse.soWhat: So what: leadership signal without a shipping signal. Track whether Fit Finder leaves beta before the next results.

pulse.headline: Maison Lumière reports 18% online conversion uplift attributed to Atelier
pulse.soWhat: So what: one of very few quantified AI ROI figures stated on a call rather than briefed to press. Use it as the benchmark others get measured against.

pulse.headline: EU AI Act transparency obligations begin applying to consumer recommendation systems
pulse.soWhat: So what: hits Orbit Commerce hardest, since ranking is the product. Everyone else has a disclosure question, not a redesign question.

pulse.headline: Bellamy & Co discloses €40m annualised saving from supply-chain models
pulse.soWhat: So what: efficiency framing with a real number beats moat framing without one. Cite this when a board asks what good looks like.
